title: Lazy-Lacquer Sichuan Fish Bao
description: A yeasty, glassy-jelly Sichuan dish featuring fish stock and lacquer-glaze, perfect for a lazy Sunday. This egg-free-friendly recipe is easy to make and packed with flavor.

ingredients.name: Lacquer-glaze (maple syrup, hoisin sauce, rice vinegar)

instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the warm water and yeast, and let it sit for 5 minutes until frothy.
Add the flour, fish stock cube, scallions, Sichuan pepper, cornstarch, salt, and black pepper to the bowl, and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on the size you prefer for your bao.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten it slightly into a disk shape.
Brush the tops with the lacquer-glaze and make a few cuts on the surface to allow steam to escape.
Place the bao on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving about 1 inch of space between each bao.
Brush the tops with vegetable oil and bake for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
While the bao are baking, mix the fermented bean paste with a little water to create a paste.
Once the bao are done, let them cool for a few minutes before serving with the fermented bean paste.
